featured_reviews.name: 光頭小伍
featured_reviews.review_text:
走進孟買的心臟，你會來到一個讓世界又震撼又敬佩的地方——Dharavi。這裡面積僅約1.75平方公里，卻容納了數十萬人口，是亞洲最密集的社區之一。但如果你只用「貧民窟」來定義它，那就太小看這裡了。

在狹窄巷弄之間，藏著驚人的經濟能量。回收、皮革、紡織、陶器，一間間小工坊日夜運轉，創造出數億美元的產值，產品甚至銷往世界各地。這裡沒有華麗辦公室，卻有最真實的創業精神；沒有資源優勢，卻用雙手打造無限可能。

來自印度各地的人們在此落腳，不同語言、宗教與文化交織，形成獨特的生命力。儘管面對擁擠與衛生挑戰，他們依然努力生活、努力工作，用韌性撐起整個城市的運轉。

達拉維不是悲情的象徵，而是一面鏡子，讓人看見人在困境中依然可以發光。走一趟，你會重新理解什麼叫做努力，什麼叫做希望。
featured_reviews.review_translated_text:
Step into the heart of Mumbai, and you'll find a place that both shocks and inspires awe—Dharavi. Spanning only about 1.75 square kilometers, it houses hundreds of thousands of people, making it one of the most densely populated communities in Asia. But to define it merely as a "slum" would be a gross underestimation.

Hidden within its narrow alleyways is an astonishing economic energy. Recycling, leather, textiles, pottery—small workshops operate day and night, generating hundreds of millions of dollars in revenue, with products sold worldwide. Here, there are no glamorous offices, but the most genuine entrepreneurial spirit; no resource advantages, but limitless possibilities created with their own hands.

People from all over India have settled here, their diverse languages, religions, and cultures intertwining to create a unique vitality. Despite facing overcrowding and sanitation challenges, they persevere, working hard and resiliently keeping the city running.

Dharavi is not a symbol of tragedy, but a mirror reflecting the light that shines even in adversity. A visit will give you a new understanding of the meaning of hard work and hope.

Most tourists photograph Mumbai's skyline and move on. Smart travellers walk it instead. Two hours on foot through South Mumbai teaches you more than a week of taxi windows ever could.

The Mumbai Heritage Walk by Cityscape Mumbai Tours starts at Regal Cinema in Colaba and ends at Churchgate Station. On the heritage walk, guides point out its honey-colored stone, the winged figure on its gable, and the statue of Sir Pherozeshah Mehta standing guard outside. It is easy to walk past a government office. It is hard to walk past this one.

featured_reviews.name: Brett Hansen
featured_reviews.review_text:
We joined the ethical walking tour of Dharavi slums with Reality Tours & Travel and it was one of the most eye opening and meaningful experiences of our time in Mumbai, India.

Our guide Diksha was excellent. She is a young Gen Z woman who is incredibly wise, well informed and very articulate. She explained the social, economic and cultural realities of Dharavi with clarity and compassion, and was always happy to answer questions along the way.

What I appreciated most about this tour is that it focuses primarily on the businesses and industries operating within Dharavi rather than treating it like a spectacle. We saw small scale recycling operations, leather workshops, pottery areas and many other hardworking micro industries. It was fascinating to learn how much manufacturing and production takes place here. At times we also walked through incredibly narrow pathways between homes, sometimes only about a metre wide, which gave a sense of just how densely populated the area is.

Dharavi has an estimated population of between 700,000 and 1 million people living in only about 2.1 square kilometres, so the energy and activity is intense. People work extremely hard. Many workers come from other regions of India, sending money home to their families and only seeing them once or twice a year. Some sleep at their workplaces and work 12 to 15 hour days. It is a tough life and seeing this reality firsthand is humbling.

One of the most confronting things we learned is that materials produced in Dharavi are sometimes used by high end international brands. However, the origin is often labelled simply as “Made in India” rather than Dharavi because of the stigma attached to the area. That was heartbreaking to hear given the skill and effort of the people working there.

Photography and video are not allowed on the tour, which is completely fair and respectful. It keeps the focus on learning rather than treating people’s lives as a spectacle.

Another reason to support this tour is that 80 percent of the profits go back into local education programs run by the organisation. While schooling in India is compulsory, class sizes can be around one teacher to 50 students. Reality Tours supports supplementary learning including English and IT classes, along with scholarships for local students.

The tour was scheduled for about 90 minutes but ended up running for closer to two hours and fifteen minutes, so we were definitely tired by the end, but it was absolutely worth it.

If you want to better understand a part of Mumbai that many visitors never see, this slum tour is thoughtful, respectful and genuinely educational. It reminds you that there are whole worlds of experience beyond our own daily lives, and that they are worth learning about with empathy and respect.

Nina and David

featured_reviews.review_text:
Had an amazing stay at this hostel! Everything was excellent—from the facilities and cleanliness to the friendly atmosphere. The staff were welcoming and always helpful, making the experience even better.

featured_reviews.name: ila ramesh
featured_reviews.review_text:
stayed at Hammock Hostels during our Mumbai trip and absolutely loved the experience! The entire place had such a calm and homely atmosphere. The staff deserves special appreciation, especially Arjun, who was incredibly sweet, helpful, and friendly with every single guest. He really knows how to make people feel comfortable and welcomed 🌸
For a hostel located in a premium area like Bandra/Khar, the pricing and facilities were surprisingly good. Everything a traveller would need was available, from comfortable dorms to relaxing common spaces. We especially loved the small library area and the open space near the kitchen where guests could sit, chat, and unwind.
Even the mixed dorm experience turned out to be completely comfortable because all the inmates were respectful, cooperative, and pleasant to be around. The whole vibe of the hostel felt safe, peaceful, and positive.
This place truly felt less like a hostel and more like a home away from home. We had such a lovely stay and would happily recommend it to anyone visiting Mumbai ✨

featured_reviews.name: Mona Seipelt
featured_reviews.review_text: The hostel has a really unique and familiar atmosphere. That staff make you feel very comfortable and welcome. There are some activities that you can book, breakfast and chai sometime. It is cleaned very well every day and even in summer times the rooms are nice and cool. I felt very safe as a female traveler also in a mixed dorm and going out alone in that area. The only down side is the smelling of fish due to a fish market close by. For me that was very manageable though. Highly recommend this hostel.

featured_reviews.name: Nagaraj Hallur
featured_reviews.review_text:
One of the best place i have stayed. Considering Mumbai as a fast moving city and equally chaotic, this place was the abode which made my stay beautiful.
I was here for work in Mumbai and thanks to Arjun who made my stay worth it and fun. The breakfast setup at the terrace is great, cleanliness standards are way higher than any other hostels in india I've stayed at.

featured_reviews.name: Alphoncy Mani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Staying at Hammock Hostels was honestly one of the best parts of my Mumbai trip. The vibe is super chill and welcoming. The staff made me feel at home from minute one and helped with everything

*What I loved:*
- *Clean & comfy*: Beds were clean, AC worked great, and the lockers gave peace of mind.
- *Social scene*: The common area and rooftop are perfect for meeting fellow travelers. Met some amazing people over chai.
- *Location*: In Juhu area, so close to the beach and cafes, but still quiet enough to sleep well.
- *Value for money*: For Mumbai prices, the facilities and cleanliness are a steal.

If you want a hostel that feels like a community and not just a place to crash, Hammock is it. I’d 100% stay here again.

featured_reviews.name: Dawn J. Thomas
featured_reviews.review_text:

The hostel seems to have friendly vibes and the upstairs terrace is nice. Especially if you were looking to connect with other travellers (which we were not 😉). They had a DJ playing but out of respect the music stopped by 11 pm and then the place was quite quiet.

I would definitely recommend this place as it’s in a pretty good location and the price wasn’t too bad. Also the staff are very friendly — and the vibe of the whole place has a friendly welcoming vibe.

They also happen to have one of the best rooftops in Jaipur — we even had a fireworks show from the palace across the street 🎇

featured_reviews.name: Deborah S
featured_reviews.review_text:
As the guide was a local, it was helpful to have his insights as to life in Dharavi.

Dharavi is, in reality, like a small town. There are schools, businesses, shops etc. Residents work in Dharavi, as well as travelling into local areas and the city centre for work.

The reality is that the place is very cramped - by the nature of the building. Early types of accomodation have more rooms per dwelling than later ones. For many of the later additions, it will be only one room for three or four people.

My guide was Dawaad with Amaze Mumbai Tours. He was excellent.

featured_reviews.name: Andre
featured_reviews.review_text:
Honestly the best Mumbai experience you can get if you have one day in the city. Don’t bother to try go on your own.

Rahul is a very friendly guide with a lot of knowledge and strong local background.
Tour is highly recommended for anyone who wants to see all sides of Mumbai in one day.

It was well planned and organized tour with few highlights: Dharavi Slum, local bazaar, Gandhi Muzeum, local souvenir shops or lunch at famous Leopold Cafe. It took around 8-9 hours and was truly great experience (100% safe, fair and professional).

featured_reviews.name: Vladyslava Yeremeieva
featured_reviews.review_text: It was the best experience in Mumbai for me and my group of 7 friends. Thanks to Rahul for quick response, lucky us booked an excursion 2h before.  Our guide   Mayur is very profesional and did his best for us! We’ve seen… EVERYTHING! We are very impressed, especially of the conditions people live and how happy they are! People there are so smily, friendly and warm. Please do not be afraid to go for this experience, it definitely worths it. You will be shocked, but it is really not bad small, not a lot trash, no dangerous people etc. We did slum excursion, had a pottery lesson and beatiful ladies did henna for us. Guys, i wish you good luck, improve yourself and stay so happy!

featured_reviews.name: Jeffery (JP) Potvin
featured_reviews.review_text: I really enjoyed my foot tour through Dharavi!  The tour is about 2.5-3hrs with walking and meeting locals.  You have a very easy walk about 4-6km during your tour!  Along the tour we met many nice hard working local people who were very cool with sharing their day to day works in many active industries found within Dharavi, from plastics to textiles.  Pooja was our leader and exceptional guide!  She provided a real insider view into the inner workings of Dharavi, from the businesses to the locals living there!  We stopped on the street for a glass of fresh juice, made our way into a cool bag shop, while ending our tour snapping street art photos!  Highly suggest taking this tour to learn more about the inner workings of a fast-paced area in Mumbai, India!  Thank you for sharing and creating such a nice foot tour of Dharavi, Pooja!  Pooja for President!  Keep aiming high and keep going for it! :)  #rockstar #india #community #Pooja #president

featured_reviews.name: Shawn Levin
featured_reviews.review_text:
Pooja (the first female tour guide of the slums) was waiting for me in the lobby of my hotel with a giant smile on her face right on time. We hopped in the car and we're off.  I hadn't been in Mumbai for more than an hour and  now I'm in the bustle of traffic to a new adventure

Pooja was very happy and fun to be with. Her accommodating personality made it feel like a stroll with a friend more than a guide.

Upon arrival she showed me a nice coffee place before we entered the slum which was enough to recharge the batteries after the long flight in.

I had little expectations and learned a lot. Everyone along the wall was happy and friendly. She showed me the lifecycle of plastic and discussed what it was like growing up there. We saw the industrial and residential districts and got to meet and talk to many people along the way.

It was a delightful experience and if you can get Pooja, I would highly recommend. As a person who has seen many parts of the world, this was memorable and I'm happy to have gone.

featured_reviews.name: Rob Steele
featured_reviews.review_text:
On my very first visit to Mumbai (& in fact India) I was put in contact with Mumbai By Locals by my Hotel and was lucky enough to have Mubeen show up for my City tour to introduce me to the metro area. What a fantastic and personable guide he is-It’s like being taken on a tour with a long lost friend! Mubeen and his driver showed up spot on time and really listened to what I was interested in seeing. He instantly on the fly (over a Masala Chai Tea) at the first stop devised a brilliant itinerary for the next few hours.
